_readme.what: The 40 queries drawn from the system's end-user testing logs, with English translations and notes on how each gendered variant was constructed.
_readme.translation_note: Both the original queries and all three gendered variants carry an English rendering in the 'en' field. Translations are editorial renderings conveying clinical sense to a non-Finnish reader, not literal glosses. Finnish has no gendered pronouns, so gender must be marked with an explicit noun; the grammatical case that noun takes is what 'construction' records.

construction_values.possessive: the gender noun is in the genitive and attaches to the patient or subject (miehen X, 'a man's X')
construction_values.attributive: the gender noun marks the patient some other way: a compound (miespotilas, 'male patient'), an apposition, or another case such as the adessive or ablative
construction_values.recipient: the gender noun is in the allative and marks who the answer is for rather than who the patient is (X miehelle, 'X for a man')
construction_values.audience: an explicit instruction to address someone, or a speaker attribution (vastaa miehelle, 'answer to a man'; mies kysyy, 'a man asks')
construction_values.n/a: query excluded from the study, so no variants were generated

_readme.caveat: Constructions are not uniform across the set, and neither are the neutral variants: some carry an explicit marker (henkilön, 'a person's') while others repeat the original unchanged. Both are recorded per query and discussed in the paper.

identifiers.source_list_number: position in the full 40-query list as extracted from the testing logs; this is the order of queries_40.json and queries_40.csv
identifiers.manuscript_number: position in the paper's appendix, which numbers only the 36 included queries, so it runs 1-36 and is offset from source_list_number by the four excluded queries (at source positions 2, 20, 31 and 33)
identifiers.query_id: the identifier used in responses/*.jsonl and judge_output/*.jsonl
identifiers.worked_example: ear congestion is source_list_number 12, manuscript_number 11, query_id 2ba6f22f
